def coning_correction(alpha_prev: np.ndarray, alpha: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Body rotation vector over one IMU interval, with the coning correction.

    Adds to the integrated gyro output the coning term of Savage's
    one-sample-plus-previous algorithm, which estimates from the previous
    interval's increment how much the rotation axis turned within this one.

    Args:
        alpha_prev: Attitude increment alpha_ib^b of the previous
            interval, shape (3,) [rad]; zeros at the first interval.
        alpha: Attitude increment alpha_ib^b of this interval, the
            integral of omega_ib^b over it, shape (3,) [rad].

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: Rotation vector of the body relative to inertial
            space over the interval, shape (3,) [rad].

    Examples:
        A rotation about a fixed axis has no coning:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import coning_correction
        >>> coning_correction(np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.1]), np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.1])).tolist()
        [0.0, 0.0, 0.1]
    """
    # --8<-- [start:coning]
    return alpha + _cross(alpha_prev, alpha) / 12.0

docs.title: sculling_correction
docs.text:
sculling_correction(alpha_prev: ndarray, upsilon_prev: ndarray, alpha: ndarray, upsilon: ndarray) -> ndarray

Velocity increment over one IMU interval, with rotation and sculling corrections.

Resolves the integrated accelerometer output in the body axes at the start of the interval. The rotation term accounts for the body turning while the specific force is integrated; the sculling term (Savage's one-sample-plus-previous algorithm) for rotation and specific force oscillating together within the interval.

Parameters:

  • alpha_prev (ndarray) –

    Attitude increment of the previous interval, shape (3,) [rad]; zeros at the first interval.

  • upsilon_prev (ndarray) –

    Specific-force increment of the previous interval, shape (3,) [m/s]; zeros at the first interval.

  • alpha (ndarray) –

    Attitude increment alpha_ib^b of this interval, shape (3,) [rad].

  • upsilon (ndarray) –

    Specific-force increment upsilon_ib^b of this interval, the integral of f_ib^b over it, shape (3,) [m/s].

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    numpy.ndarray: Specific-force velocity increment resolved in the body axes at the start of the interval, shape (3,) [m/s].

Examples:

Rolling through 0.1 rad while sensing 1 m/s along the body y axis turns part of that increment towards z:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import sculling_correction
>>> zero = np.zeros(3)
>>> sculling_correction(zero, zero, np.array([0.1, 0.0, 0.0]),
...                     np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])).tolist()
[0.0, 1.0, 0.05]
Source code in ins_sim/navigation/strapdown.py 
def sculling_correction(alpha_prev: np.ndarray, upsilon_prev: np.ndarray,
                        alpha: np.ndarray, upsilon: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Velocity increment over one IMU interval, with rotation and sculling corrections.

    Resolves the integrated accelerometer output in the body axes at the
    start of the interval. The rotation term accounts for the body turning
    while the specific force is integrated; the sculling term (Savage's
    one-sample-plus-previous algorithm) for rotation and specific force
    oscillating together within the interval.

    Args:
        alpha_prev: Attitude increment of the previous interval, shape (3,)
            [rad]; zeros at the first interval.
        upsilon_prev: Specific-force increment of the previous interval,
            shape (3,) [m/s]; zeros at the first interval.
        alpha: Attitude increment alpha_ib^b of this interval, shape (3,)
            [rad].
        upsilon: Specific-force increment upsilon_ib^b of this interval,
            the integral of f_ib^b over it, shape (3,) [m/s].

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: Specific-force velocity increment resolved in the
            body axes at the start of the interval, shape (3,) [m/s].

    Examples:
        Rolling through 0.1 rad while sensing 1 m/s along the body y axis
        turns part of that increment towards z:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import sculling_correction
        >>> zero = np.zeros(3)
        >>> sculling_correction(zero, zero, np.array([0.1, 0.0, 0.0]),
        ...                     np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])).tolist()
        [0.0, 1.0, 0.05]
    """
    # --8<-- [start:sculling]
    rotation = 0.5 * _cross(alpha, upsilon)
    sculling = (_cross(alpha_prev, upsilon) + _cross(upsilon_prev, alpha)) / 12.0
    return upsilon + rotation + sculling

docs.text:
strapdown_navgrade(meas_omega_ib_b: ndarray, meas_f_ib_b: ndarray, init_state: NavState | Sequence, tau_i: float, meas_h_b: ndarray | None = None, baro_tau: float = 100.0, mechanization: Literal['basic', 'precision'] = 'basic') -> NavSolution

Runs local-level (NED) strapdown integration with rotating-Earth corrections.

Each step (Groves notation):

  1. Evaluate omega_ie^n, omega_en^n and g(L_b, h_b) at the current state.
  2. Body rate relative to the navigation frame: omega_nb^b = omega_ib^b − C_n^b·(omega_ie^n + omega_en^n).
  3. Update C_b^n with the exact rotation-vector exponential of omega_nb^b·tau_i.
  4. Resolve specific force into NED: f_ib^n = C_b^n·f_ib^b.
  5. Velocity update, forward Euler: dv_eb^n/dt = f_ib^n − (2·omega_ie^n + omega_en^n) × v_eb^n + g_b^n.
  6. Curvilinear position update, forward Euler.

With mechanization="precision" the IMU outputs are read as the increments of an integrating IMU, alpha_ib^b = omega·tau_i and upsilon_ib^b = f·tau_i, and steps 2 to 6 become:

  • Attitude: C_b^n(+) = exp(−[omega_in^n·tau_i ×])·C_b^n(−)·exp([phi ×]), with phi from coning_correction.
  • Velocity: the increment from sculling_correction, resolved in NED with the start attitude and corrected for half the nav frame's rotation over the interval, replaces f_ib^n·tau_i.
  • Position: the trapezoidal rule on the velocities at both ends.

Parameters:

  • meas_omega_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Gyro output, angular rate of the body relative to inertial space resolved in body axes, shape (M, 3) [rad/s].

  • meas_f_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Accelerometer output, specific force resolved in body axes, shape (M, 3) [m/s²].

  • init_state (NavState | Sequence) –

    Initial state (L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n): a NavState, or any sequence of those five values in that order.

  • tau_i (float) –

    Integration interval [s].

  • meas_h_b (ndarray | None, default: None ) –

    Optional barometric height measurement, shape (M,) [m]. When provided it drives a third-order baro-damped vertical channel: the INS-minus-baro height residual feeds proportional corrections into the height and vertical-velocity updates plus an integral state that absorbs steady vertical accelerometer error. This stabilises the inherently unstable vertical channel of a free-inertial navigator (the +√(2g/R) eigenvalue from the free-air gravity gradient). When None the vertical channel runs free-inertial and diverges accordingly. Defaults to None.

  • baro_tau (float, default: 100.0 ) –

    Time constant of the baro-damping loop [s]; the three gains place a triple pole at −1/baro_tau. Only used when meas_h_b is given. Defaults to 100.0.

  • mechanization (Literal['basic', 'precision'], default: 'basic' ) –

    "basic" (the steps above, first order in tau_i) or "precision" (coning, rotation and sculling corrections and a trapezoidal position update). Defaults to "basic".

Returns:

  • NavSolution ( NavSolution ) –

    (r_lb_l, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n) at every sample; unpacks positionally in that order.

Examples:

A level IMU at rest senses only Earth rate and gravity, and the navigator stays exactly at rest:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
>>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import earth_rate_n, normal_gravity
>>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import NavState, strapdown_navgrade
>>> L_b = np.deg2rad(45.0)
>>> gyro = np.tile(earth_rate_n(L_b), (100, 1))
>>> accel = np.tile([0.0, 0.0, -normal_gravity(L_b, 0.0)], (100, 1))
>>> start = NavState(L_b, 0.0, 0.0, np.zeros(3), Rotation.identity().as_quat())
>>> nav = strapdown_navgrade(gyro, accel, start, tau_i=0.1)
>>> float(np.abs(nav.v_eb_n).max())
0.0

def strapdown_navgrade(meas_omega_ib_b: np.ndarray, meas_f_ib_b: np.ndarray,
                       init_state: NavState | Sequence, tau_i: float,
                       meas_h_b: np.ndarray | None = None,
                       baro_tau: float = 100.0,
                       mechanization: Literal["basic", "precision"] = "basic",
                       ) -> NavSolution:
    """Runs local-level (NED) strapdown integration with rotating-Earth corrections.

    Each step (Groves notation):

    1. Evaluate omega_ie^n, omega_en^n and g(L_b, h_b) at the current state.
    2. Body rate relative to the navigation frame:
       `omega_nb^b = omega_ib^b − C_n^b·(omega_ie^n + omega_en^n)`.
    3. Update C_b^n with the exact rotation-vector exponential of
       omega_nb^b·tau_i.
    4. Resolve specific force into NED: `f_ib^n = C_b^n·f_ib^b`.
    5. Velocity update, forward Euler:
       `dv_eb^n/dt = f_ib^n − (2·omega_ie^n + omega_en^n) × v_eb^n + g_b^n`.
    6. Curvilinear position update, forward Euler.

    With `mechanization="precision"` the IMU outputs are read as the
    increments of an integrating IMU, alpha_ib^b = omega·tau_i and
    upsilon_ib^b = f·tau_i, and steps 2 to 6 become:

    - Attitude: `C_b^n(+) = exp(−[omega_in^n·tau_i ×])·C_b^n(−)·exp([phi ×])`,
      with phi from `coning_correction`.
    - Velocity: the increment from `sculling_correction`, resolved in NED
      with the start attitude and corrected for half the nav frame's
      rotation over the interval, replaces f_ib^n·tau_i.
    - Position: the trapezoidal rule on the velocities at both ends.

    Args:
        meas_omega_ib_b: Gyro output, angular rate of the body relative to
            inertial space resolved in body axes, shape (M, 3) [rad/s].
        meas_f_ib_b: Accelerometer output, specific force resolved in body
            axes, shape (M, 3) [m/s²].
        init_state: Initial state (L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n): a
            NavState, or any sequence of those five values in that order.
        tau_i: Integration interval [s].
        meas_h_b: Optional barometric height measurement, shape (M,) [m].
            When provided it drives a third-order baro-damped vertical
            channel: the INS-minus-baro height residual feeds proportional
            corrections into the height and vertical-velocity updates plus
            an integral state that absorbs steady vertical accelerometer
            error. This stabilises the inherently unstable vertical channel
            of a free-inertial navigator (the +√(2g/R) eigenvalue from the
            free-air gravity gradient). When None the vertical channel runs
            free-inertial and diverges accordingly. Defaults to None.
        baro_tau: Time constant of the baro-damping loop [s]; the three
            gains place a triple pole at −1/baro_tau. Only used when
            meas_h_b is given. Defaults to 100.0.
        mechanization: "basic" (the steps above, first order in tau_i) or
            "precision" (coning, rotation and sculling corrections and a
            trapezoidal position update). Defaults to "basic".

    Returns:
        NavSolution: (r_lb_l, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n) at every
            sample; unpacks positionally in that order.

    Examples:
        A level IMU at rest senses only Earth rate and gravity, and the
        navigator stays exactly at rest:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
        >>> from ins_sim.core.earth_model import earth_rate_n, normal_gravity
        >>> from ins_sim.navigation.strapdown import NavState, strapdown_navgrade
        >>> L_b = np.deg2rad(45.0)
        >>> gyro = np.tile(earth_rate_n(L_b), (100, 1))
        >>> accel = np.tile([0.0, 0.0, -normal_gravity(L_b, 0.0)], (100, 1))
        >>> start = NavState(L_b, 0.0, 0.0, np.zeros(3), Rotation.identity().as_quat())
        >>> nav = strapdown_navgrade(gyro, accel, start, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> float(np.abs(nav.v_eb_n).max())
        0.0
    """
    M = len(meas_omega_ib_b)
    L_b = np.zeros(M); lambda_b = np.zeros(M); h_b = np.zeros(M)
    v_eb_n = np.zeros((M, 3)); q_b_n = np.zeros((M, 4))
    r_lb_l = np.zeros((M, 3))          # for plotting against truth

    L_b[0], lambda_b[0], h_b[0], v_eb_n[0], q_b_n[0] = init_state
    C_b_n = Rot.from_quat(q_b_n[0])
    L_b0 = L_b[0]                      # reference for the local NED display
    h_b0 = h_b[0]
    R_N0, R_E0 = wgs84_radii(L_b0)     # loop-invariant: L_b0 never changes
    g_b_n = np.zeros(3)                # reused each iteration
    if mechanization not in ("basic", "precision"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown mechanization: {mechanization!r}")
    precision = mechanization == "precision"
    alpha_prev = np.zeros(3)           # previous interval's increments,
    upsilon_prev = np.zeros(3)         # for the precision mechanization

    # --8<-- [start:baro_gains]
    # Third-order baro-damping gains: triple pole at -1/baro_tau for the
    # (height error, vertical-velocity error, accel-error integrator) loop.
    if meas_h_b is not None:
        K1 = 3.0 / baro_tau
        K2 = 3.0 / baro_tau ** 2
        K3 = 1.0 / baro_tau ** 3
        acc_corr = 0.0                 # integral state [m/s²], → -δa_D
    # --8<-- [end:baro_gains]

    for k in range(M - 1):
        # --8<-- [start:frame_rates]
        # --- 1. Local rotating-Earth quantities at step k --------------
        omega_ie_n = earth_rate_n(L_b[k])
        omega_en_n = transport_rate_n(v_eb_n[k], L_b[k], h_b[k])
        omega_in_n = omega_ie_n + omega_en_n                   # nav-frame rate
        g_b_n[2] = normal_gravity(L_b[k], h_b[k])
        # --8<-- [end:frame_rates]

        if precision:
            # --8<-- [start:precision_midpoint]
            # The nav-frame rate, gravity and Coriolis at the middle of the
            # interval, extrapolated from this step and the previous one.
            gravity_coriolis = g_b_n - _cross(2.0 * omega_ie_n + omega_en_n, v_eb_n[k])
            if k == 0:
                omega_in_prev, gravity_coriolis_prev = omega_in_n, gravity_coriolis
            omega_in_mid = 1.5 * omega_in_n - 0.5 * omega_in_prev
            gravity_coriolis_mid = 1.5 * gravity_coriolis - 0.5 * gravity_coriolis_prev
            omega_in_prev, gravity_coriolis_prev = omega_in_n, gravity_coriolis
            # --8<-- [end:precision_midpoint]

            # --8<-- [start:precision_attitude]
            alpha = meas_omega_ib_b[k] * tau_i                 # alpha_ib^b
            upsilon = meas_f_ib_b[k] * tau_i                   # upsilon_ib^b
            zeta = omega_in_mid * tau_i                        # nav-frame rotation
            phi = coning_correction(alpha_prev, alpha)
            C_b_n_next = Rot.from_rotvec(-zeta) * C_b_n * Rot.from_rotvec(phi)
            # --8<-- [end:precision_attitude]
            q_b_n[k+1] = C_b_n_next.as_quat() # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]

            # --8<-- [start:precision_velocity]
            dv_b = sculling_correction(alpha_prev, upsilon_prev, alpha, upsilon)
            dv_sf_n = C_b_n.apply(dv_b) - 0.5 * _cross(zeta, C_b_n.apply(upsilon))
            v_eb_n[k+1] = v_eb_n[k] + dv_sf_n + gravity_coriolis_mid * tau_i
            # --8<-- [end:precision_velocity]
            if meas_h_b is not None:
                baro_residual = h_b[k] - meas_h_b[k]
                v_eb_n[k+1, 2] += (K2 * baro_residual + acc_corr) * tau_i
                acc_corr += K3 * baro_residual * tau_i

            # --8<-- [start:precision_position]
            R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b[k])
            h_b[k+1] = h_b[k] - 0.5 * (v_eb_n[k, 2] + v_eb_n[k+1, 2]) * tau_i
            L_pred = L_b[k] + v_eb_n[k, 0] / (R_N + h_b[k]) * tau_i
            R_N_next, R_E_next = wgs84_radii(L_pred)
            L_b[k+1] = L_b[k] + 0.5 * (v_eb_n[k, 0] / (R_N + h_b[k])
                                       + v_eb_n[k+1, 0] / (R_N_next + h_b[k+1])) * tau_i
            lambda_b[k+1] = lambda_b[k] + 0.5 * (
                v_eb_n[k, 1] / ((R_E + h_b[k]) * np.cos(L_b[k]))
                + v_eb_n[k+1, 1] / ((R_E_next + h_b[k+1]) * np.cos(L_b[k+1]))) * tau_i
            # --8<-- [end:precision_position]
            if meas_h_b is not None:
                h_b[k+1] -= K1 * baro_residual * tau_i

            r_lb_l[k+1, 0] = (L_b[k+1] - L_b0) * (R_N0 + h_b0)
            r_lb_l[k+1, 1] = (lambda_b[k+1] - lambda_b[0]) * (R_E0 + h_b0) * np.cos(L_b0)
            r_lb_l[k+1, 2] = -(h_b[k+1] - h_b0)
            alpha_prev, upsilon_prev = alpha, upsilon
            C_b_n = C_b_n_next
            continue

        # --8<-- [start:body_rate]
        # --- 2. Body rate relative to the nav frame ------------------
        # The gyro saw omega_ib^b. Subtract the nav frame's own rotation
        # (resolved in body axes) to get what drives the b→n attitude update.
        C_n_b = C_b_n.inv()
        omega_nb_b = meas_omega_ib_b[k] - C_n_b.apply(omega_in_n)
        # --8<-- [end:body_rate]

        # --8<-- [start:attitude_update]
        # --- 3. Attitude update (exact rotation-vector exponential) ---
        dC = Rot.from_rotvec(omega_nb_b * tau_i)
        C_b_n_next = C_b_n * dC                                # right-mult: body increment
        q_b_n[k+1] = C_b_n_next.as_quat() # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
        # --8<-- [end:attitude_update]

        # --8<-- [start:specific_force_transform]
        # --- 4. Specific force in NED (forward Euler — consistent with
        #        the truth IMU, which uses the same first-order scheme) ---
        f_ib_n = C_b_n.apply(meas_f_ib_b[k])
        # --8<-- [end:specific_force_transform]

        # --8<-- [start:velocity_update]
        # --- 5. Rotating-frame velocity update ------------------------
        coriolis = np.cross(2.0 * omega_ie_n + omega_en_n, v_eb_n[k])
        v_eb_n_dot = f_ib_n - coriolis + g_b_n
        # Baro damping: the height residual corrects vertical velocity
        # (K2) and updates the accel-error integrator (K3); a positive
        # residual (INS high) commands positive Down velocity.
        if meas_h_b is not None:
            baro_residual = h_b[k] - meas_h_b[k]
            v_eb_n_dot[2] += K2 * baro_residual + acc_corr
            acc_corr += K3 * baro_residual * tau_i
        v_eb_n[k+1] = v_eb_n[k] + v_eb_n_dot * tau_i
        # --8<-- [end:velocity_update]

        # --8<-- [start:position_update]
        # --- 6. Curvilinear position (forward Euler — matches truth) --
        R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b[k])
        L_b[k+1] = L_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k][0] / (R_N + h_b[k])) * tau_i
        lambda_b[k+1] = lambda_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k][1] /
                                       ((R_E + h_b[k]) * np.cos(L_b[k]))) * tau_i
        h_b[k+1] = h_b[k] - v_eb_n[k][2] * tau_i
        if meas_h_b is not None:
            h_b[k+1] -= K1 * baro_residual * tau_i
        # --8<-- [end:position_update]

        # Position relative to the start point (for plotting against
        # truth): linearized curvilinear-to-metres conversion using the
        # start-point radii R_N0, R_E0.
        # --8<-- [start:relative_position]
        r_lb_l[k+1, 0] = (L_b[k+1] - L_b0) * (R_N0 + h_b0)
        r_lb_l[k+1, 1] = (lambda_b[k+1] - lambda_b[0]) * (R_E0 + h_b0) * np.cos(L_b0)
        r_lb_l[k+1, 2] = -(h_b[k+1] - h_b0)
        # --8<-- [end:relative_position]

        C_b_n = C_b_n_next

    return NavSolution(r_lb_l, L_b, lambda_b, h_b, v_eb_n, q_b_n)

docs.text: The sensor error models: the datasheet parameters and the noisy gyro, accelerometer and barometer outputs they produce.

docs.title: ins_sim.sensors.imu
docs.text:
IMU error model: datasheet parameters and simulated gyro and accelerometer outputs.

An IMUSpec, usually loaded from YAML with load_imu_spec, sets the spread of each error term in the Groves (2013) sensor model:

meas_f_ib_b     = b_a + (I + M_a)·f_ib_b     + w_a
meas_omega_ib_b = b_g + (I + M_g)·omega_ib_b + w_g

generate_imu_samples draws one realization of these errors along a truth trajectory, and draw_initial_misalignment draws the initial alignment error. The model is explained on the IMU error model theory page, and its symbols on Notation & conventions.

docs.title: GM_ALLAN_PEAK module-attribute
docs.text:
GM_ALLAN_PEAK = 0.6173642831

Peak of the Allan deviation of a first-order Gauss-Markov process, per unit of its spread.

The peak occurs at an averaging time of 1.8926 correlation times. ins_sim models bias instability with such a process and sets its steady-state spread σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK, so that the simulated bias's Allan deviation peaks at the datasheet bias instability B.

docs.title: IMUSpec dataclass
docs.text:
IMUSpec(gyro_arw: float = 0.002 * pi / 180 / 60, gyro_bias_instability: float = 0.01 * pi / 180 / 3600, gyro_bias_tau: float = 3600.0, gyro_br_std: float = 0.01 * pi / 180 / 3600, gyro_sf_std: float = 0.0, gyro_ma_std: float = 0.0, accel_vrw: float = 0.005 / 60, accel_bias_instability: float = 5e-06 * 9.80665, accel_bias_tau: float = 3600.0, accel_br_std: float = 2.5e-05 * 9.80665, accel_sf_std: float = 0.0, accel_ma_std: float = 0.0, align_tilt_std: float = 0.0, align_heading_std: float = 0.0, baro: BaroSpec | None = None)

Navigation-grade IMU error parameters, as quoted on a sensor datasheet.

The defaults are typical of fielded navigation-grade systems, such as a ring-laser-gyro aircraft INS:

Parameter Gyro Accelerometer Random walk (ARW, VRW) 0.002 °/√h 0.005 m/s/√h Bias instability 0.01 °/h 5 µg Turn-on repeatability 0.01 °/h 25 µg

Every field is a datasheet parameter in SI units; each one sets the spread of a Groves (2013) error term (see the Notation & conventions page). Bias instability is the datasheet value, the floor of the sensor's Allan deviation. The in-run bias is simulated as a first-order Gauss-Markov process whose steady-state spread (gyro_gm_std, accel_gm_std) is chosen so that its Allan deviation peaks at exactly that value.

Attributes:

  • gyro_arw (float) –

    Gyro angular random walk, the density of the white noise w_g [rad/√s].

  • gyro_bias_instability (float) –

    Gyro bias instability from the datasheet, the floor of the Allan deviation [rad/s]. Sets the dynamic bias b_gd.

  • gyro_bias_tau (float) –

    Correlation time of the Gauss-Markov process that models the gyro bias instability [s].

  • gyro_br_std (float) –

    Gyro turn-on bias repeatability, the std dev of the static bias b_gs [rad/s].

  • gyro_sf_std (float) –

    Gyro scale-factor error std dev (diagonal of M_g), drawn once per run per axis [dimensionless, e.g. 5e-6 = 5 ppm].

  • gyro_ma_std (float) –

    Gyro axis-misalignment std dev (off-diagonal of M_g), drawn once per run per element [rad].

  • accel_vrw (float) –

    Accelerometer velocity random walk, the density of the white noise w_a [(m/s)/√s].

  • accel_bias_instability (float) –

    Accelerometer bias instability from the datasheet, the floor of the Allan deviation [m/s²]. Sets the dynamic bias b_ad.

  • accel_bias_tau (float) –

    Correlation time of the Gauss-Markov process that models the accelerometer bias instability [s].

  • accel_br_std (float) –

    Accelerometer turn-on bias repeatability, the std dev of the static bias b_as [m/s²].

  • accel_sf_std (float) –

    Accelerometer scale-factor error std dev (diagonal of M_a) [dimensionless].

  • accel_ma_std (float) –

    Accelerometer axis-misalignment std dev (off-diagonal of M_a) [rad].

  • align_tilt_std (float) –

    Initial-alignment tilt (N/E) error std dev [rad]. Physically ≈ accel repeatability / g.

  • align_heading_std (float) –

    Initial-alignment heading (azimuth) error std dev [rad]. Physically ≈ gyrocompass limit, gyro repeatability / (omega_ie·cos L_b).

  • baro (BaroSpec | None) –

    Errors of the barometric altimeter that aids the vertical channel (see ins_sim.sensors.baro.BaroSpec), or None for an ideal barometer that reports the true height.

Note

The multiplicative (scale factor, misalignment) and initial-alignment terms default to zero, and the barometer to ideal — they apply only when specified — so zero-noise diagnostic specs and legacy YAMLs keep their exact-passthrough behavior.

docs.title: gyro_gm_std property
docs.text:
gyro_gm_std: float

Steady-state std dev of the gyro Gauss-Markov bias b_gd [rad/s].

Chosen so that the bias's Allan deviation peaks at gyro_bias_instability: σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK ≈ 1.62·B.

Steady-state std dev of the accelerometer Gauss-Markov bias b_ad [m/s²].

Chosen so that the bias's Allan deviation peaks at accel_bias_instability: σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK ≈ 1.62·B.

load_imu_spec(yaml_path: str) -> IMUSpec

Loads an IMUSpec from a YAML file expressed in datasheet units.

Parameters:

  • yaml_path (str) –

    Path to a YAML file with gyro and accel sections in datasheet units (deg/√hr, deg/hr, µg, etc.), and optional alignment and baro sections. Without a baro section the barometer is ideal.

Returns:

  • IMUSpec ( IMUSpec ) –

    Equivalent error-parameter set converted to SI units.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.config import default_imu_spec_path
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import load_imu_spec
>>> spec = load_imu_spec(str(default_imu_spec_path()))
>>> round(float(np.rad2deg(spec.gyro_arw) * 60), 4)   # back to °/√h
0.002
Source code in ins_sim/sensors/imu.py 
def load_imu_spec(yaml_path: str) -> IMUSpec:
    """Loads an IMUSpec from a YAML file expressed in datasheet units.

    Args:
        yaml_path: Path to a YAML file with `gyro` and `accel` sections
            in datasheet units (deg/√hr, deg/hr, µg, etc.), and optional
            `alignment` and `baro` sections. Without a `baro` section the
            barometer is ideal.

    Returns:
        IMUSpec: Equivalent error-parameter set converted to SI units.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.config import default_imu_spec_path
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import load_imu_spec
        >>> spec = load_imu_spec(str(default_imu_spec_path()))
        >>> round(float(np.rad2deg(spec.gyro_arw) * 60), 4)   # back to °/√h
        0.002
    """
    with open(yaml_path) as fh:
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(fh)
    g = cfg["gyro"]
    a = cfg["accel"]
    al = cfg.get("alignment", {})
    baro = cfg.get("baro")
    # --8<-- [start:datasheet_units]
    DEG_HR = np.pi / 180 / 3600
    return IMUSpec(
        gyro_arw     = g["arw_deg_per_rt_hr"]          * np.pi / 180 / 60,
        gyro_bias_instability = g["bias_instab_deg_per_hr"]  * DEG_HR,
        gyro_bias_tau         = g["bias_tau_s"],
        gyro_br_std  = g["repeatability_deg_per_hr"]   * DEG_HR,
        gyro_sf_std  = g.get("scale_factor_ppm", 0.0)   * 1e-6,
        gyro_ma_std  = g.get("misalignment_urad", 0.0)  * 1e-6,
        accel_vrw    = a["vrw_m_per_s_per_rt_hr"]      / 60,
        accel_bias_instability = a["bias_instab_ug"]     * 1e-6 * 9.80665,
        accel_bias_tau         = a["bias_tau_s"],
        accel_br_std = a["repeatability_ug"]            * 1e-6 * 9.80665,
        accel_sf_std = a.get("scale_factor_ppm", 0.0)   * 1e-6,
        accel_ma_std = a.get("misalignment_urad", 0.0)  * 1e-6,
        align_tilt_std    = al.get("tilt_std_deg", 0.0)    * np.pi / 180,
        align_heading_std = al.get("heading_std_deg", 0.0) * np.pi / 180,
        baro = None if baro is None else baro_spec_from_yaml(baro),
    )

docs.text:
draw_initial_misalignment(spec: IMUSpec, rng: Generator) -> ndarray

Draws a per-run initial-alignment attitude error delta_psi_nb^n.

Models the residual error of a stationary gyrocompass alignment: small tilts about North/East (limited by accelerometer bias over g) and a larger azimuth error about Down (limited by east-gyro bias over omega_ie·cos L_b). Apply as C_b^n(estimated) = exp([delta_psi_nb^n ^])·C_b^n(true).

Parameters:

  • spec (IMUSpec) –

    IMU error-parameter set (align_tilt_std, align_heading_std).

  • rng (Generator) –

    Seeded NumPy random generator.

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    numpy.ndarray: Attitude error rotation vector resolved in NED, [North tilt, East tilt, Down (heading)], shape (3,) [rad].

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec, draw_initial_misalignment
>>> spec = IMUSpec(align_tilt_std=1e-5, align_heading_std=7e-4)
>>> draw_initial_misalignment(spec, np.random.default_rng(0)).shape
(3,)

def draw_initial_misalignment(spec: IMUSpec,
                              rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draws a per-run initial-alignment attitude error delta_psi_nb^n.

    Models the residual error of a stationary gyrocompass alignment:
    small tilts about North/East (limited by accelerometer bias over g)
    and a larger azimuth error about Down (limited by east-gyro bias
    over omega_ie·cos L_b). Apply as C_b^n(estimated) =
    exp([delta_psi_nb^n ^])·C_b^n(true).

    Args:
        spec: IMU error-parameter set (align_tilt_std,
            align_heading_std).
        rng: Seeded NumPy random generator.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: Attitude error rotation vector resolved in NED,
            [North tilt, East tilt, Down (heading)], shape (3,) [rad].

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec, draw_initial_misalignment
        >>> spec = IMUSpec(align_tilt_std=1e-5, align_heading_std=7e-4)
        >>> draw_initial_misalignment(spec, np.random.default_rng(0)).shape
        (3,)
    """
    # --8<-- [start:initial_misalignment]
    return rng.normal(0.0, [spec.align_tilt_std,
                            spec.align_tilt_std,
                            spec.align_heading_std])

docs.title: generate_imu_samples
docs.text:
generate_imu_samples(truth: TruthTrajectory, spec: IMUSpec, rng: Generator) -> IMUSamples

Generates noisy IMU samples from a truth trajectory and an error spec.

Per-axis IMU model (Groves notation):

meas_f_ib_b     = b_a + (I + M_a)·f_ib_b     + w_a
meas_omega_ib_b = b_g + (I + M_g)·omega_ib_b + w_g
  • M_a, M_g: scale factor (diagonal) and misalignment (off-diagonal), drawn once per run.
  • b_as, b_gs: static (turn-on) bias ~ N(0, σ_BR²), drawn once per run.
  • b_ad, b_gd: dynamic bias, a first-order Gauss-Markov process with correlation time τ and steady-state spread σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK, so that its Allan deviation peaks at the datasheet bias instability B. Stationary from t = 0.
  • w_a, w_g: white noise, with σ = VRW/√tau_i or ARW/√tau_i per sample.

The gyro and accelerometer triads draw from separate random streams spawned from rng, so changing one triad's parameters leaves the other's error realization unchanged.

Parameters:

  • truth (TruthTrajectory) –

    Truth trajectory exposing t, tau_i, omega_ib_b (shape (M, 3) [rad/s]) and f_ib_b (shape (M, 3) [m/s²]).

  • spec (IMUSpec) –

    IMU error-parameter set.

  • rng (Generator) –

    Seeded NumPy random generator. Two child streams are spawned from it, one per sensor triad.

Returns:

  • IMUSamples ( IMUSamples ) –

    (meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b), the noisy gyro and accelerometer outputs, each shape (M, 3).

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec, generate_imu_samples
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
>>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
>>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
>>> imu = generate_imu_samples(truth, IMUSpec(), np.random.default_rng(1))
>>> imu.meas_omega_ib_b.shape == truth.omega_ib_b.shape
True
Source code in ins_sim/sensors/imu.py 
def generate_imu_samples(truth: "TruthTrajectory", spec: IMUSpec,
                         rng: np.random.Generator) -> IMUSamples:
    """Generates noisy IMU samples from a truth trajectory and an error spec.

    Per-axis IMU model (Groves notation):

        meas_f_ib_b     = b_a + (I + M_a)·f_ib_b     + w_a
        meas_omega_ib_b = b_g + (I + M_g)·omega_ib_b + w_g

    - M_a, M_g: scale factor (diagonal) and misalignment (off-diagonal),
      drawn once per run.
    - b_as, b_gs: static (turn-on) bias ~ N(0, σ_BR²), drawn once per run.
    - b_ad, b_gd: dynamic bias, a first-order Gauss-Markov process with
      correlation time τ and steady-state spread σ = B / GM_ALLAN_PEAK, so
      that its Allan deviation peaks at the datasheet bias instability B.
      Stationary from t = 0.
    - w_a, w_g: white noise, with σ = VRW/√tau_i or ARW/√tau_i per sample.

    The gyro and accelerometer triads draw from separate random streams
    spawned from `rng`, so changing one triad's parameters leaves the
    other's error realization unchanged.

    Args:
        truth: Truth trajectory exposing `t`, `tau_i`, `omega_ib_b`
            (shape (M, 3) [rad/s]) and `f_ib_b` (shape (M, 3) [m/s²]).
        spec: IMU error-parameter set.
        rng: Seeded NumPy random generator. Two child streams are spawned
            from it, one per sensor triad.

    Returns:
        IMUSamples: (meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b), the noisy gyro and
            accelerometer outputs, each shape (M, 3).

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.imu import IMUSpec, generate_imu_samples
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
        >>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
        >>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> imu = generate_imu_samples(truth, IMUSpec(), np.random.default_rng(1))
        >>> imu.meas_omega_ib_b.shape == truth.omega_ib_b.shape
        True
    """
    tau_i = truth.tau_i
    rng_gyro, rng_accel = rng.spawn(2)
    meas_omega_ib_b = _triad_measurement(
        rng_gyro, truth.omega_ib_b, tau_i, spec.gyro_sf_std, spec.gyro_ma_std,
        spec.gyro_br_std, spec.gyro_gm_std, spec.gyro_bias_tau, spec.gyro_arw)
    meas_f_ib_b = _triad_measurement(
        rng_accel, truth.f_ib_b, tau_i, spec.accel_sf_std, spec.accel_ma_std,
        spec.accel_br_std, spec.accel_gm_std, spec.accel_bias_tau, spec.accel_vrw)
    return IMUSamples(meas_omega_ib_b, meas_f_ib_b)

docs.title: ins_sim.sensors.baro
docs.text:
Barometric altimeter error model: the height measurement that aids the vertical channel.

A pressure altimeter converts static pressure to height through a standard atmosphere, so its errors come from the atmosphere differing from that standard, not from the sensor alone (Groves 2013, Chapter 6). A BaroSpec sets the spread of each error term in the model

meas_h_b = h_b + s_b·(h_b − h_b0) + b_bs + b_bd(t) + w_b

and generate_baro_samples draws one realization of it along a truth trajectory. The model is explained on the Vertical channel theory page.

docs.title: BaroSpec dataclass
docs.text:
BaroSpec(scale_factor_std: float = 0.0, bias_std: float = 0.0, drift_std: float = 0.0, drift_tau: float = 3600.0, noise_density: float = 0.0)

Barometric altimeter error parameters, in SI units.

Every spread defaults to zero, so BaroSpec() is an ideal barometer that reports the true height.

Attributes:

  • scale_factor_std (float) –

    Std dev of the scale-factor error s_b, drawn once per run [dimensionless, e.g. 0.02 = 2%]. Models a non-standard air temperature: the altimeter's height above the departure point is off by s_b times that height.

  • bias_std (float) –

    Std dev of the static bias b_bs, drawn once per run [m]. Models the error in the altimeter setting (QNH) and the sensor's own offset.

  • drift_std (float) –

    Steady-state std dev of the drift b_bd, a first-order Gauss-Markov process [m]. Models the weather: the sea-level pressure changing along the route and over time.

  • drift_tau (float) –

    Correlation time of the drift [s], above 0.

  • noise_density (float) –

    Density of the white noise w_b [m·√s, i.e. m/√Hz]. The per-sample std dev is noise_density/√tau_i, so the noise the vertical channel sees does not depend on the time step.

def baro_spec_from_yaml(cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> BaroSpec:
    """Converts the `baro:` block of an IMU spec YAML file to a BaroSpec.

    Args:
        cfg: The parsed block, in datasheet units. Every key is optional
            and defaults to no error: `scale_factor_pct` [%], `bias_m` [m],
            `drift_m` [m], `drift_tau_s` [s, default 3600] and
            `noise_m_per_rt_hz` [m/√Hz].

    Returns:
        BaroSpec: The same parameters in SI units.

    Examples:
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.baro import baro_spec_from_yaml
        >>> baro_spec_from_yaml({"scale_factor_pct": 2.0, "bias_m": 10.0})
        BaroSpec(scale_factor_std=0.02, bias_std=10.0, drift_std=0.0, drift_tau=3600.0, noise_density=0.0)
    """
    # --8<-- [start:datasheet_units]
    return BaroSpec(
        scale_factor_std = cfg.get("scale_factor_pct", 0.0) / 100.0,
        bias_std         = cfg.get("bias_m", 0.0),
        drift_std        = cfg.get("drift_m", 0.0),
        drift_tau        = cfg.get("drift_tau_s", 3600.0),
        noise_density    = cfg.get("noise_m_per_rt_hz", 0.0),
    )

docs.title: generate_baro_samples
docs.text:
generate_baro_samples(truth: TruthTrajectory, spec: BaroSpec, rng: Generator) -> ndarray

Generates barometric height measurements from a truth trajectory.

Measurement model:

meas_h_b = h_b + s_b·(h_b − h_b0) + b_bs + b_bd(t) + w_b
  • s_b: scale-factor error ~ N(0, scale_factor_std²), drawn once per run. It scales the height above the departure point h_b0, where the altimeter setting makes the barometer read correctly apart from b_bs.
  • b_bs: static bias ~ N(0, bias_std²), drawn once per run.
  • b_bd: drift, a stationary first-order Gauss-Markov process with spread drift_std and correlation time drift_tau.
  • w_b: white noise, with σ = noise_density/√tau_i per sample.

The draws come from rng in a fixed order (s_b, b_bs, the drift, w_b) whatever the parameter values, so changing one spread never reshuffles the others.

Parameters:

  • truth (TruthTrajectory) –

    Truth trajectory exposing h_b (shape (M,) [m]) and tau_i.

  • spec (BaroSpec) –

    Barometer error-parameter set.

  • rng (Generator) –

    Seeded NumPy random generator.

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    numpy.ndarray: Measured height meas_h_b, shape (M,) [m].

Examples:

An ideal barometer reports the true height:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.baro import BaroSpec, generate_baro_samples
>>> truth = SimpleNamespace(h_b=np.array([100.0, 150.0, 200.0]), tau_i=1.0)
>>> generate_baro_samples(truth, BaroSpec(), np.random.default_rng(0))
array([100., 150., 200.])
Source code in ins_sim/sensors/baro.py 
def generate_baro_samples(truth: "TruthTrajectory", spec: BaroSpec,
                          rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Generates barometric height measurements from a truth trajectory.

    Measurement model:

        meas_h_b = h_b + s_b·(h_b − h_b0) + b_bs + b_bd(t) + w_b

    - s_b: scale-factor error ~ N(0, scale_factor_std²), drawn once per
      run. It scales the height above the departure point h_b0, where the
      altimeter setting makes the barometer read correctly apart from b_bs.
    - b_bs: static bias ~ N(0, bias_std²), drawn once per run.
    - b_bd: drift, a stationary first-order Gauss-Markov process with
      spread drift_std and correlation time drift_tau.
    - w_b: white noise, with σ = noise_density/√tau_i per sample.

    The draws come from `rng` in a fixed order (s_b, b_bs, the drift, w_b)
    whatever the parameter values, so changing one spread never reshuffles
    the others.

    Args:
        truth: Truth trajectory exposing `h_b` (shape (M,) [m]) and `tau_i`.
        spec: Barometer error-parameter set.
        rng: Seeded NumPy random generator.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: Measured height meas_h_b, shape (M,) [m].

    Examples:
        An ideal barometer reports the true height:

        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.baro import BaroSpec, generate_baro_samples
        >>> truth = SimpleNamespace(h_b=np.array([100.0, 150.0, 200.0]), tau_i=1.0)
        >>> generate_baro_samples(truth, BaroSpec(), np.random.default_rng(0))
        array([100., 150., 200.])
    """
    h_b = np.asarray(truth.h_b, dtype=float)
    tau_i = truth.tau_i
    # --8<-- [start:baro_errors]
    s_b = rng.normal(0.0, spec.scale_factor_std)
    b_bs = rng.normal(0.0, spec.bias_std)
    b_bd = gauss_markov(rng, len(h_b), tau_i, spec.drift_std, spec.drift_tau,
                        n_axes=1)[:, 0]
    w_b = rng.normal(0.0, spec.noise_density / np.sqrt(tau_i), size=len(h_b))
    return h_b + s_b * (h_b - h_b[0]) + b_bs + b_bd + w_b

docs.title: ins_sim.sensors.noise
docs.text:
Random processes shared by the sensor error models.

gauss_markov draws the first-order Gauss-Markov process that ins_sim uses for every slowly wandering sensor error: the in-run bias of the gyros and accelerometers, and the weather drift of the barometric altimeter.

docs.title: gauss_markov
docs.text:
gauss_markov(rng: Generator, n_samples: int, tau_i: float, sigma: float, tau_c: float, n_axes: int = 3) -> ndarray

Draws a stationary first-order Gauss-Markov process on each axis.

The discrete recursion is

x[k+1] = a·x[k] + √(1 − a²)·σ·u[k+1],   a = exp(−tau_i/tau_c),

with u white and unit-variance. The process starts in its stationary distribution, x[0] ~ N(0, σ²), so its spread is σ at every sample and its autocorrelation is exp(−|Δt|/tau_c).

The draws come from rng in a fixed order, x[0] then u, and happen whatever σ is, so a zero σ consumes the same random numbers as any other value.

Parameters:

  • rng (Generator) –

    Seeded NumPy random generator.

  • n_samples (int) –

    Number of samples M.

  • tau_i (float) –

    Sample interval [s].

  • sigma (float) –

    Steady-state standard deviation σ, in the process's units.

  • tau_c (float) –

    Correlation time [s], above 0.

  • n_axes (int, default: 3 ) –

    Number of independent axes. Defaults to 3.

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    numpy.ndarray: The process, shape (n_samples, n_axes).

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from ins_sim.sensors.noise import gauss_markov
>>> x = gauss_markov(np.random.default_rng(0), 5, tau_i=1.0,
...                  sigma=2.0, tau_c=60.0, n_axes=1)
>>> x.shape
(5, 1)
Source code in ins_sim/sensors/noise.py 
def gauss_markov(rng: np.random.Generator, n_samples: int, tau_i: float,
                 sigma: float, tau_c: float, n_axes: int = 3) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draws a stationary first-order Gauss-Markov process on each axis.

    The discrete recursion is

        x[k+1] = a·x[k] + √(1 − a²)·σ·u[k+1],   a = exp(−tau_i/tau_c),

    with u white and unit-variance. The process starts in its stationary
    distribution, x[0] ~ N(0, σ²), so its spread is σ at every sample and
    its autocorrelation is exp(−|Δt|/tau_c).

    The draws come from `rng` in a fixed order, x[0] then u, and happen
    whatever σ is, so a zero σ consumes the same random numbers as any
    other value.

    Args:
        rng: Seeded NumPy random generator.
        n_samples: Number of samples M.
        tau_i: Sample interval [s].
        sigma: Steady-state standard deviation σ, in the process's units.
        tau_c: Correlation time [s], above 0.
        n_axes: Number of independent axes. Defaults to 3.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: The process, shape (n_samples, n_axes).

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from ins_sim.sensors.noise import gauss_markov
        >>> x = gauss_markov(np.random.default_rng(0), 5, tau_i=1.0,
        ...                  sigma=2.0, tau_c=60.0, n_axes=1)
        >>> x.shape
        (5, 1)
    """
    # --8<-- [start:gauss_markov]
    # The IIR filter produces the zero-start response to u; the decaying
    # initial state a^k·x[0] is added to it.
    a = np.exp(-tau_i / tau_c)
    s = np.sqrt(1.0 - a * a) * sigma
    x0 = rng.normal(0.0, sigma, size=n_axes)
    u = rng.normal(size=(n_samples, n_axes)); u[0] = 0.0
    return (lfilter([1.0], [1.0, -a], s * u, axis=0)
            + a ** np.arange(n_samples)[:, None] * x0)

docs.title: Trajectory
docs.text: The truth trajectory, built from a mission YAML or a spline path, and the outputs a perfect IMU would produce along it.

docs.title: ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics
docs.text:
Truth trajectory: the reference motion, and what a perfect IMU measures along it.

build_trajectory builds a TruthTrajectory from a mission YAML, phase by phase; TruthTrajectory.from_spline builds one by flying a spline path at constant speed. Either way the truth carries the curvilinear position, velocity and attitude at every sample, plus the outputs a perfect gyro (omega_ib_b) and accelerometer (f_ib_b) would produce.

Those IMU outputs are derived as the exact inverse of the strapdown mechanization's update, so feeding them back through the navigator reproduces the truth to numerical precision. That zero-noise round trip checks the consistency of the two halves; it does not measure how accurately the mechanization integrates continuous motion. See the Truth trajectory & ideal IMU theory page.

docs.title: TruthTrajectory
docs.text:
TruthTrajectory(pos_profile: ndarray, v_eb_n: ndarray, euler_nb: ndarray, tau_i: float, L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49, h_b0: float = 100.0, oversample: int | None = None)

Truth state derived from a raw kinematic profile, consistent with rotating-Earth navigation kinematics.

Computed at every sample (Groves notation):

  • Position relative to the start point, r_lb^l (linearized geodetic reprojection, so it is directly comparable to the strapdown output).
  • Velocity v_eb^n (input) and its time derivative (numerical).
  • Curvilinear position (L_b, lambda_b, h_b), integrated from the start.
  • Euler angles (input).
  • Angular rate omega_ib^b that a perfect gyro would output. This includes Earth rate and transport rate, resolved in body axes, via the exact discrete body-to-NED rotation.
  • Specific force f_ib^b that a perfect accelerometer would output, derived from the forward-difference rotating-frame velocity equation so that a forward-Euler strapdown recovers the truth exactly.

Attributes:

  • tau_i (float) –

    Sample interval [s].

  • t (ndarray) –

    Time vector, shape (M,) [s].

  • r_lb_l (ndarray) –

    Position relative to the start point, resolved in the start point's NED axes, shape (M, 3) [m].

  • v_eb_n (ndarray) –

    Velocity of the body relative to the Earth, resolved in NED, shape (M, 3) [m/s].

  • v_eb_n_dot (ndarray) –

    Time derivative of v_eb_n (central differences, diagnostic only), shape (M, 3) [m/s²].

  • L_b (ndarray) –

    Geodetic latitude, shape (M,) [rad].

  • lambda_b (ndarray) –

    Longitude, shape (M,) [rad].

  • h_b (ndarray) –

    Geodetic height, shape (M,) [m].

  • euler_nb (ndarray) –

    Euler angles [phi_nb (roll), theta_nb (pitch), psi_nb (heading)], shape (M, 3) [rad].

  • C_b_n (Rotation) –

    Body-to-NED attitude C_b^n, vectorized over all M samples.

  • omega_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Truth gyro output omega_ib^b, shape (M, 3) [rad/s].

  • f_ib_b (ndarray) –

    Truth accelerometer output f_ib^b, shape (M, 3) [m/s²].

  • g (ndarray) –

    Local gravity magnitude g(L_b, h_b), shape (M,) [m/s²].

  • oversample (int | None) –

    Profile samples per IMU interval for integrated IMU outputs, or None for the exact inverse of the basic strapdown update.

Builds the truth trajectory from raw position/velocity/Euler-angle profiles.

Parameters:

  • pos_profile (ndarray) –

    Raw NED position profile, shape (M, 3) [m]. Only used to determine the sample count; the exposed r_lb_l attribute is recomputed from the integrated curvilinear position (see class docstring).

  • v_eb_n (ndarray) –

    Velocity profile resolved in NED, shape (M, 3) [m/s].

  • euler_nb (ndarray) –

    Euler angles [roll, pitch, heading], shape (M, 3) [rad].

  • tau_i (float) –

    Sample interval [s].

  • L_b0_deg (float, default: 38.97 ) –

    Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.

  • lambda_b0_deg (float, default: -76.49 ) –

    Initial longitude [deg]. Defaults to -76.49.

  • h_b0 (float, default: 100.0 ) –

    Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.

  • oversample (int | None, default: None ) –

    When None (the default) the IMU outputs are the exact inverse of the basic strapdown update, as described above. When an integer M, the profiles are sampled M times per IMU interval, at tau_i/M, and the truth is the continuous motion through them: the body turns at a constant rate and the velocity changes at a constant rate between profile samples. The IMU outputs are the averages of omega_ib^b and f_ib^b over each interval tau_i, as an integrating IMU reports them, and the states are kept every M-th sample.

def __init__(self, pos_profile: np.ndarray, v_eb_n: np.ndarray,
             euler_nb: np.ndarray, tau_i: float,
             L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49,
             h_b0: float = 100.0, oversample: int | None = None):
    """Builds the truth trajectory from raw position/velocity/Euler-angle profiles.

    Args:
        pos_profile: Raw NED position profile, shape (M, 3) [m]. Only
            used to determine the sample count; the exposed `r_lb_l`
            attribute is recomputed from the integrated curvilinear
            position (see class docstring).
        v_eb_n: Velocity profile resolved in NED, shape (M, 3) [m/s].
        euler_nb: Euler angles [roll, pitch, heading], shape (M, 3)
            [rad].
        tau_i: Sample interval [s].
        L_b0_deg: Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.
        lambda_b0_deg: Initial longitude [deg]. Defaults to -76.49.
        h_b0: Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.
        oversample: When None (the default) the IMU outputs are the
            exact inverse of the basic strapdown update, as described
            above. When an integer M, the profiles are sampled M times
            per IMU interval, at tau_i/M, and the truth is the continuous
            motion through them: the body turns at a constant rate and
            the velocity changes at a constant rate between profile
            samples. The IMU outputs are the averages of omega_ib^b and
            f_ib^b over each interval tau_i, as an integrating IMU
            reports them, and the states are kept every M-th sample.
    """
    if oversample is not None:
        self._init_integrating(v_eb_n, euler_nb, tau_i, int(oversample),
                               np.deg2rad(L_b0_deg), np.deg2rad(lambda_b0_deg), h_b0)
        return
    self.oversample = None
    self.tau_i = tau_i
    L_b0 = np.deg2rad(L_b0_deg)
    lambda_b0 = np.deg2rad(lambda_b0_deg)

    M = len(pos_profile)
    self.t = np.arange(M) * tau_i
    self.v_eb_n = v_eb_n
    self.v_eb_n_dot = np.gradient(v_eb_n, tau_i, axis=0)
    self.euler_nb = euler_nb

    # ---- Curvilinear position by integration --------------------------
    # Integrate (L_b, lambda_b, h_b) using current radii of curvature.
    # Inherently sequential (L_b[k+1] depends on L_b[k]), so this stays
    # a loop.
    # --8<-- [start:truth_position]
    L_b = np.zeros(M); lambda_b = np.zeros(M); h_b = np.zeros(M)
    L_b[0], lambda_b[0], h_b[0] = L_b0, lambda_b0, h_b0
    for k in range(M - 1):
        R_N, R_E = wgs84_radii(L_b[k])
        L_b[k+1] = L_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k, 0] / (R_N + h_b[k])) * tau_i
        lambda_b[k+1] = lambda_b[k] + (v_eb_n[k, 1] /
                                       ((R_E + h_b[k]) * np.cos(L_b[k]))) * tau_i
        h_b[k+1] = h_b[k] - v_eb_n[k, 2] * tau_i
    # --8<-- [end:truth_position]
    self.L_b, self.lambda_b, self.h_b = L_b, lambda_b, h_b

    # Body-to-NED attitude as a vectorized scipy Rotation stack
    # --8<-- [start:attitude_from_euler]
    self.C_b_n = Rot.from_euler(
        'ZYX', np.column_stack([euler_nb[:, 2], euler_nb[:, 1], euler_nb[:, 0]]))
    # --8<-- [end:attitude_from_euler]
    C_n_b = self.C_b_n.inv()

    # ---- Truth IMU outputs (exact discrete, vectorized) --------------
    # Consistent with strapdown_navgrade's forward-Euler recursion:
    #   omega_ib_b[k] = exact discrete rotation vector C[k]→C[k+1] / tau_i
    #                   plus Earth/transport rate in body axes
    #   f_ib_b[k]     = forward-difference specific force in NED,
    #                   rotated to body axes:
    #                     f_ib_n[k] = (v[k+1]-v[k])/tau_i + Coriolis[k] - g[k]
    omega_ie_n = earth_rate_n(L_b)                       # (M, 3)
    omega_en_n = transport_rate_n(v_eb_n, L_b, h_b)      # (M, 3)
    g = normal_gravity(L_b, h_b)                         # (M,)
    self.g = g
    g_b_n = np.zeros((M, 3)); g_b_n[:, 2] = g

    # --8<-- [start:truth_specific_force]
    v_eb_n_rate = np.empty((M, 3))
    v_eb_n_rate[:-1] = (v_eb_n[1:] - v_eb_n[:-1]) / tau_i
    v_eb_n_rate[-1]  = v_eb_n_rate[-2]
    f_ib_n = v_eb_n_rate + np.cross(2.0 * omega_ie_n + omega_en_n, v_eb_n) - g_b_n
    self.f_ib_b = C_n_b.apply(f_ib_n)
    # --8<-- [end:truth_specific_force]

    # --8<-- [start:truth_angular_rate]
    dC_b = self.C_b_n[:-1].inv() * self.C_b_n[1:]       # C_b(k+1)^b(k)
    omega_nb_b_fwd = dC_b.as_rotvec() / tau_i            # (M-1, 3)
    omega_nb_b = np.vstack([omega_nb_b_fwd, omega_nb_b_fwd[-1:]])
    self.omega_ib_b = omega_nb_b + C_n_b.apply(omega_ie_n + omega_en_n)
    # --8<-- [end:truth_angular_rate]

    # Reproject truth position through the same linearized geodetic
    # formula that strapdown_navgrade uses, so error =
    # estimated r_lb_l - truth.r_lb_l measures actual navigation error
    # rather than flat-earth vs. curved-earth bias.
    R_N0, R_E0 = wgs84_radii(L_b0)
    r_lb_l = np.zeros((M, 3))
    r_lb_l[:, 0] = (L_b - L_b0)   * (R_N0 + h_b0)
    r_lb_l[:, 1] = (lambda_b - lambda_b[0]) * (R_E0 + h_b0) * np.cos(L_b0)
    r_lb_l[:, 2] = -(h_b - h_b0)
    self.r_lb_l = r_lb_l

from_spline(path: NEDSplinePath, speed: float, tau_i: float, L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49, h_b0: float = 100.0, oversample: int | None = None) -> TruthTrajectory

Builds a truth trajectory by traversing a spline path at constant speed.

Parameters:

  • path (NEDSplinePath) –

    NED spline path to traverse.

  • speed (float) –

    Along-path speed [m/s], assumed constant.

  • tau_i (float) –

    Sample interval [s].

  • L_b0_deg (float, default: 38.97 ) –

    Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.

  • lambda_b0_deg (float, default: -76.49 ) –

    Initial longitude [deg]. Defaults to -76.49.

  • h_b0 (float, default: 100.0 ) –

    Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.

  • oversample (int | None, default: None ) –

    Profile samples per IMU interval for an integrating IMU; see TruthTrajectory. Defaults to None. When set, the path stops at the last whole profile step, up to one step short of its end.

Returns:

  • TruthTrajectory ( TruthTrajectory ) –

    Truth trajectory over the spline.

Examples:

A 5 km leg flown due north at 100 m/s:

>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
>>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
>>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [5000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
>>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
>>> [round(float(v), 6) for v in truth.v_eb_n[100]]
[100.0, 0.0, 0.0]

@classmethod
def from_spline(cls, path: NEDSplinePath, speed: float, tau_i: float,
                 L_b0_deg: float = 38.97, lambda_b0_deg: float = -76.49,
                 h_b0: float = 100.0,
                 oversample: int | None = None) -> "TruthTrajectory":
    """Builds a truth trajectory by traversing a spline path at constant speed.

    Args:
        path: NED spline path to traverse.
        speed: Along-path speed [m/s], assumed constant.
        tau_i: Sample interval [s].
        L_b0_deg: Initial geodetic latitude [deg]. Defaults to 38.97.
        lambda_b0_deg: Initial longitude [deg]. Defaults to -76.49.
        h_b0: Initial geodetic height [m]. Defaults to 100.0.
        oversample: Profile samples per IMU interval for an integrating
            IMU; see `TruthTrajectory`. Defaults to None. When set, the
            path stops at the last whole profile step, up to one step
            short of its end.

    Returns:
        TruthTrajectory: Truth trajectory over the spline.

    Examples:
        A 5 km leg flown due north at 100 m/s:

        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.kinematics import TruthTrajectory
        >>> from ins_sim.trajectory.spline import NEDSplinePath
        >>> path = NEDSplinePath([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [5000.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
        >>> truth = TruthTrajectory.from_spline(path, speed=100.0, tau_i=0.1)
        >>> [round(float(v), 6) for v in truth.v_eb_n[100]]
        [100.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    """
    T = path.length / speed
    tau_p = tau_i / (oversample or 1)                  # profile interval
    if oversample is None:
        t = np.arange(0.0, T + tau_p, tau_p)
    else:
        # Drop the partial last interval: clamping it reverses the velocity.
        t = np.arange(int(np.floor(T / tau_p + 1e-9)) + 1) * tau_p
    s_of_t = np.minimum(speed * t, path.length)
    pos_profile = path.position(s_of_t)
    # An oversampled truth is integrated sample by sample, so first-order
    # differences at the ends would show up as a jump in roll there.
    edge_order = 1 if oversample is None else 2
    v_eb_n = np.gradient(pos_profile, tau_p, axis=0, edge_order=edge_order)
    # Coordinated-turn bank uses local gravity at the start; for short
    # trajectories using a mean g is well within the rounding error
    # of the heading-rate derivative itself.
    g_ref = normal_gravity(np.deg2rad(L_b0_deg), h_b0)
    euler_nb = _euler_from_velocity(v_eb_n, tau_p, g_ref, edge_order)
    return cls(pos_profile, v_eb_n, euler_nb, tau_i,
               L_b0_deg=L_b0_deg, lambda_b0_deg=lambda_b0_deg, h_b0=h_b0,
               oversample=oversample)
